rv.q: David Farley’s doll’s-house-style cross-section set, which splits the hotel into colour-coded quarters in the first act, is glorious, but his designs grow fussy and over-dressed in act two and leave one craving the ingenious minimalism of Operati...
The whole thing’s a visual treat; montages dangling Lance down a lift shaft, and spinning Douglas in a washing machine, are particularly inspired.
Even for Mischief, this is an ambitious show, with rarely a pause in the action.
This is an evening of daft, uncomplicated fun.
This is clearly going to be an enormous popular hit.
This finely tuned machine of comic timing and theatrical chaos is possibly Mischief’s best work yet, offering audiences exactly what they have come to expect – and love – from this troupe.

cn.t: The Play That Goes Wrong team delivers another crowd-pleasing farce with sharp wordplay and physical comedy. Critics praise the Cold War spy romp as clever, fun entertainment that honors classic British farce traditions.
